guards: LAYER 3 of 3. Canonical bytes are guarded by canonical-bytes-vectors.json; identifier spelling by packages/sdk-ts/scripts/check-parity.ts; observable BEHAVIOUR — parsed fields, error semantics, pure computation, boundary inputs, outgoing request shape and transport policy — by this file. A method can pass both other gates and still answer differently in each language; every defect this fixture was built from did exactly that.
authored_by: Hand-authored, not generated. Unlike canonical-bytes-vectors.json there is no server oracle for most of this layer: the expectations are written from the documented contract, then cross-checked against BOTH implementations. Where the two disagreed, the disagreement is recorded as a named sdk_ts_skip/sdk_py_skip carrying the observed value on each side — never silently resolved in favour of whichever language was measured first.

conventions.input: Arguments in wire spelling (snake_case). A key ABSENT from `input` means the argument is not passed at all; a key present with value null means null is passed explicitly.
conventions.exchange: The single stubbed HTTP response every request in the case receives: {status, json|text|absent, headers}. Absent `exchange` means the case must not reach the transport.
conventions.expect.request: Asserted only when present, and then exactly one request must have been issued. `method` and `path` are compared against the percent-encoded request target; `query` against the DECODED name->value map (values are strings); `raw_query` — when present — against the encoded query string character for character; `body` against the parsed JSON entity (null for no body); `headers_absent` names headers that must not be present, case-insensitively.
conventions.expect.no_request: true asserts the transport was never touched.
conventions.expect.result: Normalised return value. Only the keys named here are compared, recursively; a null expectation means the field is null OR absent, which is how a language with dataclass fields and a language with plain objects are compared at all.
conventions.expect.error: The call must raise. Only the keys named here are compared. `type: "agenttool_error"` means an instance of the SDK's AgentToolError base (subclasses count). `message_contains` is a substring assertion for messages whose exact wording is deliberately not frozen.
conventions.sdk_ts_skip / sdk_py_skip: A case that language cannot satisfy today. The loader emits a NAMED SKIP carrying this reason. Never a silent omission — silent omission is exactly how this bug class survived.

normalisation.absent_vs_null: Both loaders normalise a missing field to null before comparing, so TypeScript `undefined` and an absent Python dataclass attribute read the same.
normalisation.dataclasses: sdk-py normalises dataclass instances to field maps recursively; sdk-ts objects are already plain.
normalisation.bytes: Key material is carried as base64 in `*_b64` input fields. sdk-ts decodes to Uint8Array, sdk-py to bytes. The fixture never names a native byte type.
normalisation.numbers: Compared numerically: JSON 1 and Python 1.0 are equal. Integer expectations such as Nen scores are exact.
normalisation.error_attributes: The error shape is language-neutral snake_case: code, status, hint, docs, safety, details, next_actions, x402_version, accepts, resource, extensions, payment_required, payment_response, payment_status_link, retry_after, credits_balance. Each loader maps its own spelling (TS x402Version/paymentRequired, py x402_resource) onto it.
normalisation.method_names: The fixture names operations in snake_case (`memory.delete_by_key`). Each loader's adapter table is the only place the camelCase/snake_case mapping lives.

operations.note: THE cross-language divergence this layer exists to catch, and the one it missed. Both SDKs had exactly one definition of the path-segment encoder, both were named the same, both were imported from a shared module, both passed every identifier-parity and canonical-bytes gate — and they produced different bytes. sdk-ts wrapped encodeURIComponent, whose unescaped set includes the RFC 3986 sub-delimiters ! * ' ( ); sdk-py wrapped quote(value, safe=''), which escapes all five. One id, two URLs. Nothing in the tree compared the output, so nothing saw it. The arbiter is the server, measured rather than reasoned about: a Hono app carrying the real route shapes (/v1/traces/:id, /v1/runtimes/:id/think-once, /v1/identities/:id/keys/:keyId) behind a real Caddy built from this repo's Caddyfile answers 200 with the same matched route and the same decoded c.req.param() for id!x and id%21x alike. Both spellings work, so the tie is broken by canonical spelling — and the server's own path-segment builder, api/src/services/offer-bus/adapters.ts § pathSegment, is encodeURIComponent with those same five characters escaped. sdk-py already matched it; sdk-ts was changed to.

cases.name: a-sub-delimiter-key-is-spelled-differently-on-the-wire
cases.note: OPEN DISAGREEMENT, recorded rather than resolved. The path encoder's divergence had a twin in the query position and it is still there: sdk-ts builds this query with encodeURIComponent (memory.ts § delete_by_key) and sdk-py with quote(key, safe='') (memory.py § delete_by_key), so the same key goes out as two different byte strings. Measured, both SDKs driven through a stub transport: sdk-ts sends key=vow(rest), sdk-py sends key=vow%28rest%29. The expectation below is sdk-py's, which is the spelling the server's own offer-bus § pathSegment builder uses and the one _url.ts now emits for path segments. Closing it means changing the seven encodeURIComponent query call sites in sdk-ts — memory.ts x2, economy.ts, handoff.ts, lounge.ts, love.ts, dark-continent.ts — and the corresponding sdk-py sites, and it moves the bytes an identity-authority/v1 proof binds. That is an owner's call, not a silent fix, so it is a named skip carrying both observed values.
cases.sdk_ts_skip: sdk-ts sends `key=vow(rest)`; sdk-py sends `key=vow%28rest%29`. The query encoder was not deduplicated when the path encoder was — memory.ts builds it with encodeURIComponent, memory.py with quote(key, safe=''). Both were measured through a stub transport. Unresolved by design: the fix changes the bytes an identity-authority/v1 proof binds across seven sdk-ts call sites, which is an owner's decision.
